title: Word Ladder Length
statement:
Find the length of the shortest chain that turns one word into another by changing a single letter at a time.

Contract
- `begin` and `end` are lowercase words of the same length as every word in `words`, and `begin` differs from `end`.
- A step replaces exactly one letter of the current word with a different letter; the resulting word must appear in `words`. `begin` itself does not have to be in `words`.
- Return the number of words in the shortest chain, counting both `begin` and `end`.
- Return 0 when `end` is not in `words` or no chain exists.
- `words` may contain duplicates and may contain `begin`; do not modify it.

Examples
- `ladderLength("bake", "cave", [cake, cave, base])` returns `3` via `bake -> cake -> cave`.
- `ladderLength("bake", "cane", [cake, base, cave])` returns `0` because `cane` is not listed.
- `ladderLength("lead", "gold", [load, goad, gold, mold])` returns `4`.

examples.input: begin = bake, end = cave, words = [cake, cave, base]
begin = bake, end = cane, words = [cake, base, cave]
begin = lead, end = gold, words = [load, goad, gold, mold]

hints: Every word is a node and two words are neighbours when they differ in exactly one position, so shortest chain means shortest path in an unweighted graph.
Breadth-first search finds the shortest path. Comparing every pair of words is slow; group words by patterns such as `ba*e` (one position wildcarded) so neighbours share a pattern.

Build pattern buckets once, then run a level-by-level BFS from `begin`, marking words as seen when queued and returning the level count on reaching `end`. Intended complexity: O(n * L) time and O(n * L) space for n words of length L; the benchmark treats L as a constant, so it is O(n).
inputSyntax: Input: begin word, end word, then the word list (lowercase, equal lengths), for example: bake cave cake cave base
